title.narrative: Activity under preparation Advancing Human Rights and Accountability for Conflict-Affected and Displaced Persons in Sudan

description.narrative: The Overall Objective (Impact) of this action is to advance human rights, justice, gender equality, and the rule of law in Sudan, viewing them as essential and interconnected drivers for achieving sustainable peace and development. By fostering these principles, the Action aims to create a more secure, inclusive, and equitable environment for the nation¿s long-term progress and stability. The Specifics Objectives (Outcomes) of this action are:To break the cycle of impunity, providing remedy and establishing accountability which requires the building of effective, accountable institutions and ensuring equal and inclusive access to justice in its broadest sense for all citizens. This will be achieved by ensuring that evidence of International Human Rights Law (IHRL) and International Humanitarian Law (IHL) violations against Sudan's conflict-affected and displaced persons is systematically monitored, documented, and preserved according to international standards, thereby enabling future national and international justice and accountability mechanisms.To strengthen civic space by enhancing civil society engagement, collaboration and fostering public participation.This will be achieved through targeted support to local civil society actors and initiatives in Sudan, in their efforts to monitor and document human rights violations and prepare for future justice processes, while delivering essential community services (including legal aid, psychosocial support and livelihood opportunities) to conflict-affected and displaced persons in Sudan. Support to strengthen coordination, engagement and awareness raising among relevant stakeholders will also be a key element. The Expected Results (Outputs) to be delivered by this action contributing to the corresponding Specific Objectives are: 1.1. Strengthened monitoring, documentation and reporting of IHRL and IHL violations for future justice and accountability processes by ensuring that survivor/victims of human rights violations¿ testimonies and material evidence are documented and preserved in accordance with international standards.2.1. Strengthened capacity of civil society organizations to monitor and document human rights violations, enabling the preparation for future justice and accountability processes. Key Sudanese civic actors (mainly civil society organizations and professional associations) are capacitated to peacefully advance the importance of rule of law and human rights with a strong focus on those traditionally left behind in decision-making processes, notably women, people living with disabilities, religious minorities, and youth. Increased coordination, engagement and awareness raising among relevant stakeholders.2.2. Increased access to effective support through multi-component assistance programmes providing community-led protection and justice services, legal aid, grants for livelihoods, and psychosocial support services for conflict-affected and displaced persons in Sudan: this result directly addresses the need for equal and inclusive access to justice by providing concrete legal and financial support to survivors/victims of human rights violations which helps uphold fundamental rights.
